中心极限定理最简单的表达：随机数的和随若越来越多的随机数相加在一起而变成正态分布。中心极限定理不要求独立的随机数必须来自任何特殊的分布，或者甚至随机数来自相同的分布。中心极限定理解释了为什么正态分布信号在自然中被如此广泛应用的原因。每当许多不同的随机因素互相影响，产生的概率分布曲线即变成了高斯曲线。

Propagation of uncertainty

The expression of the uncertainty uuu:

  • Absolute error Δx\Delta xΔx;
  • Relative error Δxx\frac{\Delta x}{x}xΔx​;
  • Standard deviation σ\sigmaσ. The value of a quantity and its error are then expressed as an interval x±ux\pm ux±u;
  • The most general way to characterize uncertainty is by specifying its probability distribution

Linear combination

A set of mmm functions {fk(x1,x2,…,xn)}\{f_k(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)\}{fk​(x1​,x2​,…,xn​)}, are linear combinations of nnn variables x1,x2,…,xnx_1, x_2, \dots, x_nx1​,x2​,…,xn​ with combination coefficients Ak1,Ak2,…,Akn(k=1,2,…m)A_{k1}, A_{k2}, \dots, A_{kn}\quad (k = 1, 2 ,\dots m)Ak1​,Ak2​,…,Akn​(k=1,2,…m):

fk=∑i=1nAkixi,f_k = \sum_{i=1}^{n} A_{ki}x_i,fk​=i=1∑n​Aki​xi​,

or in matrix notation,

f⃗=Ax⃗.\vec{f} = \mathbf{A} \vec{x}.f​=Ax.

x⃗=(x1,x2,…,xn)\vec{x} = (x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)x=(x1​,x2​,…,xn​), its mean value is μ\muμ, and its variance-covariance matrix is

Σx=E[(x⃗−μ)⊗(x⃗−μ)]=(σ12σ12⋯σ1nσ21σ22⋯σ2n⋮⋮⋱⋮σn1σn2⋯σn2)=(Σ11xΣ12x⋯Σ1nxΣ21xΣ22x⋯Σ2nx⋮⋮⋱⋮Σn1xΣn2x⋯Σnnx),\Sigma^x = \text{E}[(\vec{x} - \mu) \otimes (\vec{x} - \mu)] = \begin{pmatrix}{\sigma_{1}^2}&{\sigma_{12}}&{\cdots}&{\sigma_{1n}}\\{\sigma_{21}}&{\sigma_{2}^2}&{\cdots}&{\sigma_{2n}}\\{\vdots}&{\vdots}&{\ddots}&{\vdots}\\{\sigma_{n1}}&{\sigma_{n2}}&{\cdots}&{\sigma_{n}^2}\\\end{pmatrix}= \begin{pmatrix}{\Sigma^x_{11}}&{\Sigma^x_{12}}&{\cdots}&{\Sigma^x_{1n}}\\{\Sigma^x_{21}}&{\Sigma^x_{22}}&{\cdots}&{\Sigma^x_{2n}}\\{\vdots}&{\vdots}&{\ddots}&{\vdots}\\{\Sigma^x_{n1}}&{\Sigma^x_{n2}}&{\cdots}&{\Sigma^x_{nn}}\\\end{pmatrix},Σx=E[(x−μ)⊗(x−μ)]=​σ12​σ21​⋮σn1​​σ12​σ22​⋮σn2​​⋯⋯⋱⋯​σ1n​σ2n​⋮σn2​​​=​Σ11x​Σ21x​⋮Σn1x​​Σ12x​Σ22x​⋮Σn2x​​⋯⋯⋱⋯​Σ1nx​Σ2nx​⋮Σnnx​​​,

where ⊗\otimes⊗ is the outer product, and in fact, strictly speaking, the mean value μ=1n(x1+x2+⋯+xn)\mu = \frac{1}{n}(x_1 + x_2 + \dots + x_n)μ=n1​(x1​+x2​+⋯+xn​), μ⃗=(μ,μ,…,μ)T\vec{\mu} = (\mu, \mu, \dots, \mu)^{T}μ​=(μ,μ,…,μ)T, but for simplicity we use μ\muμ to replace μ⃗\vec{\mu}μ​. Then, the variance-covariance matrix Σf\Sigma^fΣf of fff is given by

Σf=E[(f⃗−E[f⃗])⊗(f⃗−E[f⃗])]=E[A(x⃗−μ)⊗A(x⃗−μ)]=AE[(x⃗−μ)⊗(x⃗−μ)]AT=AΣxAT,\begin{align*}\Sigma^f &= E[(\vec{f} - E[\vec{f}])\otimes (\vec{f} - E[\vec{f}])] = E[\mathbf{A}(\vec{x} - \mu) \otimes \mathbf{A}(\vec{x} - \mu)] \\&= \mathbf{A} E[(\vec{x} - \mu)\otimes (\vec{x} - \mu)] \mathbf{A}^T = \mathbf{A} \Sigma^x \mathbf{A}^T\end{align*}, Σf​=E[(f​−E[f​])⊗(f​−E[f​])]=E[A(x−μ)⊗A(x−μ)]=AE[(x−μ)⊗(x−μ)]AT=AΣxAT​,

where we used the defination of the outer product u⃗⊗v⃗=u⃗v⃗T\vec{u} \otimes \vec{v} = \vec{u} \vec{v}^Tu⊗v=uvT.
In component notation, the equation

Σf=AΣxAT\boxed{\mathbf{\Sigma}^f = \mathbf{A} \mathbf{\Sigma}^x \mathbf{A}^T}Σf=AΣxAT​

reads

Σijf=∑kn∑lnAikΣklxAjl.\Sigma^f_{ij} = \sum^n_k \sum^n_l A_{ik} \Sigma^x_{kl} A_{jl}.Σijf​=k∑n​l∑n​Aik​Σklx​Ajl​.

This is the most general expression for the propagation of error from one set of variables onto another. When the errors on xxx are uncorrelated, this formula simplifies to

\bo\Sigma^f_{ij} = \sum^n_k A_{ik} \Sigma^x_{kk} A_{jk},

where Σkkx=σxk2(=σk2)\Sigma^x_{kk} = \sigma^2_{x_k} (=\sigma^2_k)Σkkx​=σxk​2​(=σk2​). Note that even though (=尽管，表示已知事实) the errors on xxx may be uncorrelated, the errors on fff are in general correlated; in other words, even if (=即使，表示假设条件) Σx\Sigma^xΣx is diagonal, Σf\Sigma^fΣf is in general a full matrix.

In simpler case, the fff is scalar-valued function, a⃗\vec{a}a is a row vector:

f=∑inaixi=a⃗x⃗f = \sum^n_i a_i x_i = \vec{a} \vec{x}f=i∑n​ai​xi​=ax

σf2=Σijf=∑in∑jnaiΣijxaj=a⃗Σxa⃗T\sigma^2_f = {\Sigma}^f_{ij} = \sum^n_i \sum^n_j a_i \Sigma^x_{ij} a_j = \vec{a} \mathbf{\Sigma}^x \vec{a}^Tσf2​=Σijf​=i∑n​j∑n​ai​Σijx​aj​=aΣxaT

As we all know, the relationship between correlation coefficient ρij\rho_{ij}ρij​ and covariance σij=Cov(xi,xj)\sigma_{ij} = \text{Cov}(x_i, x_j)σij​=Cov(xi​,xj​) is:

ρij=σijσiσj\rho_{ij} = \frac{\sigma_{ij}}{\sigma_i \sigma{j}}ρij​=σi​σjσij​​

Thus,

σf2=∑in∑jnaiρijσiσjaj=∑inai2σi2+∑in∑j(j≠i)naiajρijσiσj\sigma^2_f = \sum^n_i \sum^n_j a_i \rho_{ij}\sigma_i \sigma_j a_j = \sum^n_i a_i^2 \sigma_i^2 + \sum^n_i \sum^n_{j(j\neq i)} a_i a_j \rho_{ij} \sigma_i \sigma_jσf2​=i∑n​j∑n​ai​ρij​σi​σj​aj​=i∑n​ai2​σi2​+i∑n​j(j=i)∑n​ai​aj​ρij​σi​σj​

If xxx are uncorrelated, this simplifies further to

σf2=∑inai2σi2\sigma^2_f = \sum^n_i a_i^2 \sigma_i^2σf2​=i∑n​ai2​σi2​

In the simple case of indentical coefficients aaa and variances σ\sigmaσ, we find

σf=n∣a∣σ\sigma_f = \sqrt{n} |a| \sigmaσf​=n​∣a∣σ

If fff is the arithmetic mean of (x1,x2,…,xn)(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)(x1​,x2​,…,xn​), i.e. a=1na = \frac{1}{n}a=n1​, the result is the standard error of the mean:

σf=σn\sigma_f = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}σf​=n​σ​

Non-linear combinations

When fff is a set of non-linear combination of the variables xxx, an interval propagation could be performed in order to compute intervals which contain consistent values for the variables.

In a probabilistic approach, the function fff must be linearised by approximation to a first-order Taylor series expansion. In some cases, exact formulae can be derived, which do not depend on the expansion as in the case for the exact variance of products. The Taylor expansion is:

fk≈fk0+∑in∂fk∂xixif_k \approx f^0_k + \sum^n_i \frac{\partial f_k}{\partial x_i} x_ifk​≈fk0​+i∑n​∂xi​∂fk​​xi​

where ∂fk∂xi\frac{\partial f_k}{\partial x_i}∂xi​∂fk​​ is evaluated at the mean value of all components of vector x⃗\vec{x}x. In matrix notation,

f⃗≈f⃗0+Jx⃗\vec{f} \approx \vec{f}^0 + \mathbf{J} \vec{x}f​≈f​0+Jx

Effective single body

For a non-relativistic two-body system, we define the relative coordinate

x⃗0=x⃗1−x⃗2\vec{x}_0 = \vec{x}_1 - \vec{x}_2x0​=x1​−x2​

and the ceter-of-mass coordinate

x⃗0=m1x⃗1+m2x⃗2m1+m2\vec{x}_0 = \frac{m_1 \vec{x}_1 + m_2 \vec{x}_2}{m_1 + m_2}x0​=m1​+m2​m1​x1​+m2​x2​​

and we denote by m=m1+m2m = m_1 + m2m=m1​+m2 the total mass and by μ=m1m2/m\mu = m_1 m_2 / mμ=m1​m2​/m the reduced mass. For a non-relativistic system, the second mass moment can be written as

Mij=m1x1ix1j+x2ix2j=mxCMixCMj+μx0ix0jM^{ij} = m_1 x^{i}_{1} x^{j}_{1} + x^{i}_{2} x^{j}_{2} = m x^{i}_{\text{CM}} x^{j}_{\text{CM}} + \mu x^{i}_{0} x^{j}_{0}Mij=m1​x1i​x1j​+x2i​x2j​=mxCMi​xCMj​+μx0i​x0j​

If this system is isolated and we choose the CM frame such that xCMi=0x^{i}_{\text{CM}} = 0xCMi​=0, and we are left with a single effective particle of mass μ\muμ and coordinate x0i(t)x^{i}_{0}(t)x0i​(t), the second mass moment is Mij(t)=μx0i(t)x0j(t)M^{ij}(t) = \mu x^{i}_{0}(t) x^{j}_{0}(t)Mij(t)=μx0i​(t)x0j​(t). Keplerian motion

In a closed elliptical orbit, Kepler’s third law is equivalent to:

\left<\frac{1}{r}\right> = \frac{1}{a}$$​(i.e., the average of the inverse radius can be expressed in terms of the semi-major axis).**Derivation**Radius distance is $$r(E) = a(1 - e\cos E)

Kepler’s equation is

entry.title: Primordial Black Hole Notes
entry.content:
PBH

since PBHs are usually expected to be formed before nucleosynthesis, BBN constraints on the baryon abundance do not apply to them, as they do not intervene in the nucleosynthesis of elements, and thus, can be regarded as non-baryonic DM (Carr and Kühnel, 2020).

The concept of PBHs was initially speculated by Zel’dovich and Novikov [12] and later formally proposed by Hawking and Carr [13–15] (see also [16–20]). PBHs are also fascinating as a strong candidate for providing a possible explanation for dark matter. Depending on the time of their formation, their masses can vary from the Planck mass to the mass of a supermassive black hole [21,22].(Alestas et al. PRD [2401.02314])

entry.title: EMRI Notes
entry.content:
EMRI

0 Foreword

The volume is an important parameter when considering stellar dynamics.
The term “black hole” was first employed by John Archibald Wheeler (b. 1911).

1 Massive dark objects in galactic nuclei

The active galactic nucleus (AGN) can release energy and AGNs have large luminosities (10410^4104 times that of a typical galaxy) coming from tiby bolumes (≪1pc3\ll 1 \text{pc}^3≪1pc3). They are (one of) the most powerful objects in the universe.
Hertzsprung-Russell diagram (H-R diagram), is a scatter plot of stars showing the relationship between the stars’ absolute magnitudes or luminosities and their stellar classification or effective temperatures.
Accretion is a very efficient channel for turning matter into energy. Whilst nuclear fusion reaches only a few percent, accretion can transfer almost 50% of the mass-energy of a star into energy.
ANG has a broad frequency and radius ranges for emission, so they are far out of thermal equilibrium.

  • smaller regions are hotter;
  • components of utterly different temperature can exist together.

The release of gravitational binding energy by stellar accretion on to a MBH could be the primary powerhouse of an AGN. And MBH are found at the center of galaxies and acted in the past as the engines that powered ultraluminous quasars.
The central object is indeed a MBH rather than a cluster of smaller dark objects (like neutron stars, brown dwarfs etc), which has been probed only for two galaxies: the Milky Way and NGC4258.

Stars can be swallowed whole by MBH in two ways:

  • direct plunges
  • EMRI

Only when the compact object is dense enough will it not be dirupted by the tidal forces of the MBH. (like, a neutron star, a white dwarf or a small stellar-mass black hole.)
The significance of research on EMRI using GW: we can test the theory that massive dark objects are indeed Kerr black holes as GR predicts, and not exotic objects such as boson stars, which would be the ultimate test of GR (really!? cool!) The detection of such an EMRI will allow us to do very exciting science: EMRIs will give us measurements of the masses and spins of BHs to an accuracy which is beyond that of any other astrophysical technique. Such information will tell us about cosmic evolution, about the history and growth of MBHs in the nearby universe, with unprecedented accuracy.

2 GWs as a probe to stellar dynamics and the cosmic growth of SMBHs

It’s a statistical question of feeding a MBH, not a individual event question. And when we study GWs emitted by EMRIs, we have to study stellar dynamics as well:

  • two-body relation
  • many-body-coherent or non-coherent relaxation

Most nearby bright galaxies harbour a dark, massive, compact object at their center, and the correlation between the mass of SMBH and velocity dispersion of their host galaxies is shown before. Generally, $ M \uparrow$ and σ↑\sigma \uparrowσ↑.

Signifance: EMRIs are so appealing: a set of ∼ 10510^5105 bursts of GWs radiated by one system will tell us with the utmost accuracy about the system itself, it will test general relativity, it will tell us about the distribution of dark objects in galactic nuclei and globular clusters and, thus, we will have a new understanding of the physics of the process. New phenomena, unknown and unanticipated, are likely to be discovered. And on top of this, the measure of GWs will give us very detailed information about the spin of the central MBH, which is impossible with current techniques, X-ray observation of Fe Kα\alphaα profile, due to its uncertainties. Additionally, the secondary mass and the eccentricity of the orbit will be recovered from the GW with a tiny fractional accuracy (relative error). ( ←\leftarrow← which means high accuracy)
The mass range of central MBH in the search of EMRIs for LISA is between [107,10410^7, 10^4107,104] M⊙M_\odotM⊙​, (except the rotating MBH case, where the total mass can be to a few ∼107M⊙\sim 10^7 M_\odot∼107M⊙​), due to two reasons:

  • lareger than 107M⊙10^7 M_\odot107M⊙​: the frequency of the last stable orbit (LSO) is too low to detect.
  • less than 104M⊙10^4 M_\odot104M⊙​: the signal will be quite weak unless the source is very close.

Preread: the scale of the Milky Way is ∼104\sim 10^4∼104 pc, which is 10910^9109 times larger than the distance from the Earth to the Sun (1 AU).
Galactic or cosmological dynamics The relaxation time trlxt_\text{rlx}trlx​ of galaxy is larger than Hubble time (universe age), so we can negelect the 2-body interaction, but study cosmological simulations using N-body integrators, which means the galaxy system is “collisionless”.
Cluster dynamics If we zoom in and enter the (mostly Newtonian) stellar dynamics of galatic nuclei, trlx∼108−1010t_\text{rlx} \sim 10^8 - 10^{10}trlx​∼108−1010 yrs, which is shorter than the age the system, so one has to take into account relaxation, exchange of energy and angular momentum between stars, which means this system is “collisional”.
Relativistic stellar dynamics As a reference point, the Schwarzschild radius of a 106M⊙10^6 M_\odot106M⊙​ (109M⊙10^9 M_\odot109M⊙​) is 10−7pc10^{-7}\text{pc}10−7pc (10−4pc10^{-4} \text{pc}10−4pc), the similar size as the distance from the Earth to the Sun. In this zone, generally, there are no stars (probibility is extremely small). Because this volume is so tiny. Even there are a few stars, they will quickly (too fast) merge with MBH (EMRI). This kind of system can be collisional or collisionless, depending on how many stars we have at a given time.

3 A taxonomy of orbits in galactic nuclei

Since we are interested in EMRIs, we will focus on centrophilic orbits (中心亲和轨道) and leave centrophobic orbits (中心排斥轨道) aside.

4 Two-body relaxation in galactic nuclei

In general we refer ot “collisional” to any effect leading to exchange of energy and angular momentum among stars, sometimes we use “physical collisions” to refer to real collisions between two stars.

There are 3 ways of altering the angular momentum of stars:

  1. Two-body ralaxation It’s not the most relevant effect of contributing to EMRI sources, but it’s the best-studied effect.
  2. physical collision The impact of physical collision processes fro the global evolution of the dynamics of galactic nuclei is negligible. And the probability that stellar-mass black holes physically collide is negligible.
  3. seclar effects A keplerian orbit can be described in terms of its (1) semi-major axis and (2) eccentricity. The semi-major axis is only connected to energy and, for a given semi-major axis the eccentricity is connected to the angular momentum.

Three useful time-scales:

  1. The relaxation time We can regard it as the time interval required for the velocity distribution to reach the Maxwell-Boltzmann form.
    Relaxation can redistribute orbital energy amongst stelaar-mass objects until the most massive of them (presumably stellar-mass BH) form a power-law density cusp around the MBH, n(r)∝r−γn(r) \propto r^{-\gamma}n(r)∝r−γ. Nuclei likely to host MBHs in the LISA mass range (mass≤few×106M⊙\text{mass} \le \text{few} \times 10^6 M_\odotmass≤few×106M⊙​) probably have relaxation times comparable to or less than a Hubble time, so that it is expected that their heavier stars form a steep cusp, while less massive species arrange themselves into a shallower profile.
  2. Collision time tcollt_\text{coll}tcoll​ is defined as the required mean time for the unmber of stars within a volume to be one.
  3. The corssing time This is the required time for a star to pass through the system, i.e., to cross it.

Contrary to gas dynamics, trlx>tcrosst_\text{rlx} > t_\text{cross}trlx​>tcross​.
tdyn≪trlxt_\text{dyn} \ll t_\text{rlx}tdyn​≪trlx​, which means the system can get again a virial-type equilibrium in a short time, namely it changes in a quasi-stationary way.

Dynamical friction (DF) A star which is more massive than the average will suffer from dynamical friction, which is an effect of all encounters with lighter stars, namely relaxation boils down to dynamical friction in this case.

The diffusion and loss-cone angles Learn when using.

5 “Standard” mass segregation

Only a fool tries the harder problem when he does not understand the simplest special case.
Core collapse is not just a characteristic of multi-mass systems, but has been also observed in single mass analysis.
Mass segregation produces a core-collapse of the system that happens very fast.
During core collapse, the central regions of the cluster become completely dominated by the most massive stars. But, contrary to the case of single-mass clusters, the central velocity dispersion decreases.
The presence of a small fraction of stellar remnants may greatly affect the evolution of the cluster and growth of the MBH, because they segregate to the centre, and in doing so, they expel main sequence stars from it, but, being compact, they cannot be tidally disrupted.
In the cluster, the temperature of the inner part of the cluster will rise and the temperature of other all components decreases in the late.
EMRI emits GWs all the time, but the most important bursts of energy occur at periapsis. After every 2π2\pi2π around the orbit, the semi-major axis decays a fraction proportional to the energy loss. After typically some 104−10510^4 - 10^5104−105 cycles, the small body, the CO, plunges through the horizon of the MBH and is lost. The emission of GW finishes.
One usually assumes that the mass range of MBHs of intrest in the search of EMRIs for LISA is between [104,107]M⊙[10^4, 10^7]M_\odot[104,107]M⊙​. (The sensitivity limit for non-spinning black hole is about 5×106M⊙5\times 10^6 M_\odot5×106M⊙​, but this goes up to a few times 107M⊙10^7M_\odot107M⊙​ for prograde inspirals into rapidly spinning black holes.
) Because

  • If the central MBH >107M⊙> 10^7 M_\odot>107M⊙​, then the signal, even at the LSO, will have a frequency too low for detecting the system.
  • If the central MBH >104M⊙> 10^4 M_\odot>104M⊙​, the signal will be quite weak unless the source is very close.

Laser Interferometer Space Antenna LISA

Seismic noise is one of the main expereimental challenges for ground-based detectors, which limits their sensitivity at frequencies ≤10\le 10≤10 Hz, making them insensitive to GWs from MBH systems. However, space-borne interferometric GW detectors, such as LISA, are free from the seismic noise.
Stellar-mass BBHs are detectable by LISA years to days before they reach the sensitivity window of ground-based detectors, due to the different frequency band.

3.19

EMRI formation:
dry (loss-cone)
wet
binary
BH mass of QPE, more massive BH will swallow small star, due to tidal radial is smaller.



Babak et al. and Fan et al. forecasted that there will be a few to thousands of detectable (dry) EMRIs per year by LISA and TianQin, respectively. Zwick et al. realized post-Newtonian (PN) corrections to the commonly used Peters’s formula are necessary. With PN corrections implemented, the dry EMRI rate decreases by approximately at least one order of magnitude.

FastEMRIWaveforms (FEW) package

This framework allows gravitational selfforce-based waveform models to be computed about as rapidly as kludge models, while retaining their inherent accuracy. The key observation in our approach is that only the waveform phase needs to be known to very high precision; the amplitudes of the thousands of harmonic modes in an EMRI can computed to a much lower accuracy.

Installation Issues

when I install lapack, it installed liblapack automatically. If liblapack=3.9.0 is incompatible with few, I may need to uninstall it or look for alternative solutions.

Seems like this doesn’t compact the few package.

Usage

  • fast - sparse stepping
  • slow - dense stepping

plt.contourf Coutour map
plt.contourf 是 Matplotlib 中用于绘制填充等高线图（contour plot with filled regions的函数。它与 plt.contour 类似，但 contourf 会填充等高线之间的区域，而 contour 只绘制等高线。

If we only concentrate on the case of a Schwarzschild black hole, then the AK waveform is sufficient, rather than AAK (which is better for Kerr BH).
When dealing with long-wavelength GW signals, TDI is not used. TDI is specifically designed to improve the sensitivity to high-frequency signals, but its contribution to low-frequency signals is minimal.

Semi-latus rectum (dimensionless): Initial p0p_0p0​ Must be 10≤p0≤16+2e10 \le p_0 \le 16 + 2 e10≤p0​≤16+2e, (p0p_0p0​ cannot be too large) so that frequency drift can occur, which is a significant factor that will affect the detection efficiency of the matching filter.

英语笔记本

常见单词/词组

task force 特遣部队；特别小组；专案组；突击队
yet to do sth 尚未完成sth

give rise to 引起；导致；产生
commissioning n.调试；试运行；
tag along 跟随；（vi）tag along with sb 跟随某人
in/ on /to the east of …

  • in the west/east of在…的西/东部。in 表示方位，含义是“在……之内”，有包含之意，即一个小地方处在一个大地方的范围(疆域)之内
  • on the west/east of在…的西/东面。on 表示方位，含义是“在……端/边”，即一个地方在另一个地方的某一端或某一边，两个地方只是相邻或接壤，却互不管辖。
  • to the west/east of在…以西/东。to 表示方位，含义是“在……面”，即一个地方在另一个地方的范围之外，互不管辖。尤其当两个地方相隔较远，且有湖泊、大海等区域相隔时，通常用 to。

yet to do sth 尚未完成sth

e.g. We are yet to obtain a direct detection of a GW. 我们还没有直接探测到引力波。

punctilious adj. 一丝不苟的；精密细心的；拘泥形式的

profile n.（以数量形式记录事物特点的）曲线图，数据图标。

secular adj.（天文）长期的；缓慢的

Please don’t feel compelled to stay up late or get up early for this call as it will be recorded and the link circulated afterwards. 省略被动语态助动词的用法在英语中很常见，尤其是在口语或非正式的写作中。在上下文已经很清晰的情况下，省略助动词可以让句子变得简洁。例如，“The link circulated afterwards” 这句话中的“will be”被省略。

agnostic n.不可知的，（哲学或宗教语境下）不可知论者；（学术和科技语境中）中立的，不依赖特定假设的，与模型无关的。

e.g. Our approach offers the primary advantage of being agnostic and computationally efficient.我们方法的主要优点是模型无关且计算高效。

smoking gun evidence n.铁证，确凿的证据，决定性证据。

e.g. A detection of a subsolar mass black hole by the LIGOVirgo-KAGRA (LVK) Collaboration [23–26] would provide smoking gun evidence for PBHs, as astrophysical black holes are expected to have masses larger than ∼1M⊙.

improve

及物动词 improve + sth 改进某物不及物动词 improve on/upon + sth 在...(之前的基础)上改进 e.g.This improves on Solar System and binary pulsar bounds [98,99] by factors of a few and a thousand, respectively.这个（引力子质量的）约束比来自太阳系观测和双星脉冲星的限制分别提高了几个数量级和约一千倍

然后还有一点，我要对repository里面与个人网页有关的仓库进行设置，Settings -> Pages -> Build and deployment -> Branch -> 把None修改为gh-pages（因为我在_config.yml里设置的是branch: gh-pages）

主题：butterfly

在设置主题butterfly时我参考了这篇CSDN文章。其中我采取了他的升级建议，但是并未完全理解，后续若要更换主题，可以参考理解一下。

  • 为了減少升级主题带来的不便，我们可以把主题文件夹中的 _config.yml 重命名为 _config.butterfly.yml，复制到 Hexo 根目录下与_config.yml同级。

  • Hexo会自动合并主题中的_config.yml和 _config.butterfly.yml ，如果存在同名配置，会使用_config.butterfly.yml的配置，其优先度较高。所以像和博客网址相关联的固定资料可以设置在_config.yml中，比如博客的标题、作者信息和邮箱等等资料，而和主题样式相关的配置放在 _config.butterfly.yml 中，那么在将来你想换一个主题是很方便的。

嗷，可能在终端直接用http访问github，git clone -b master https://github.com/jerryc127/hexo-theme-butterfly.git themes/butterfly，无法克隆他的仓库（很可能是网络问题，即使我使用了魔法，依然遭遇阻碍）。但是用ssh可能会好一点，不过我没有尝试，我用的是gitee，git clone -b master https://gitee.com/immyw/hexo-theme-butterfly.git themes/butterfly。

下面是一个简单的 Python 代码示例：

Hexo的相对路径问题

_config.butterfly.yml文件在hexo的根目录myBlog下，图片wallhaven-6degg7.jpg在myBlog/source/img/wallhaven-6degg7.jpg，为什么tag_img: /img/wallhaven-6degg7.jpg这里的相对路径没有写source文件夹？

  • 答：在 Hexo 中，所有的静态资源（如图片、CSS、JavaScript 文件等）通常存放在 source 目录下。对于你提供的图片路径：myBlog/source/img/wallhaven-6degg7.jpg这个路径是在 source/img/ 目录下的一个图片文件。对于 Hexo 来说，这个路径是相对于 myBlog/source/ 目录的。当 Hexo 生成网站
    时，它会将 source 目录下的内容复制到生成的 _site 目录，并保持原有的结 构。在 Hexo 配置文件中，/img/wallhaven-6degg7.jpg 是相对网站根目录的路径，而不是相对本地文件系统的路径。因此，/img/ 指的是 Hexo 网站生成后在 _site 目录中的 img 文件夹。
    简而言之，/img/ 会映射到 source/img/ 目录，在你生成的静态网站中，图片会被正确地放在 /img/ 路径下。——摘自Chatgpt
    示例图如下：(注意，这两个图片在本地用vscode查看时,使用这个路径/img/6781739288862_.pic.jpg确实无法预览，因为Hexo的相对路径与本地不同，解释如上文所述。而../img/6781739288862_.pic.jpg在本地vscode可实现预览，但在网站上无法显示（但是之前能的呀，怎么突然就不能了，头大，路径问题？）。再多插一嘴：vscode中markdown使用图片的绝对路径时无法预览，可能的原因是当你指定绝对路径，VS Code 可能会限制访问不在工作区文件夹中的文件。日后遇到必须用绝对路径的问题时，再去Chatgpt吧，现在就先不改vscode的配置（启用本地文件的支持）了。)

keywords 与 tags 的区别

在 Hexo 中，keywords 不会像 tags 那样直接在页面上显示。tags 会被展示在文章的底部或文章页面中，作为分类的一部分，便于用户查看和点击，而 keywords 主要是面向搜索引擎的优化信息，并不会直接出现在页面上。

  • 在网页源码中：keywords 会被嵌入到 HTML 页面<meta>标签里，通常位于<head>部分，用于搜索引擎索引。这对用户来说是不可见的，但对于搜索引擎的爬虫是可见的。
  • 社交媒体预览：如果你在分享文章链接时使用了社交媒体（如微博、微信等），有些平台可能会通过 meta 信息获取文章的摘要、标题和关键词。尽管它不会像 tags 那样显示在文章页，但它可能会影响到社交媒体平台上文章的呈现。

总结来说，keywords 主要是在 SEO（Search Engine Optimization，搜索引擎优化）方面发挥作用，不会直接在你的网站页面上显示给访客，主要还是服务于搜索引擎。

数学公式渲染

我最终选择了katex。
我尝试了mathjax，但是很多教程（比如butterfly官方文档）会提示下载hexo-renderer-kramed --save，但因为这个渲染器很多年没人维护（见这位博主的描述），所以安装后会提示有五个漏洞，并且以我目前的能力无法解决。而且，听说无法很好地显示多行公式。不选择mathjax的主要原因是很久没人维护了。
所以我选择了katex，根据butterfly官方文档或者这位博主的方法，可以进行katex配置，二者的区别的插件不同，但我没有进行详细对比，效果相似。我选择的是后者，@neilsustc/markdown-it-katex。

还有一个很重要的问题，我并没有完全搞清楚。在网页上，$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ 可以被渲染为公式 a2+b2=c2a^2 + b^2 = c^2a2+b2=c2，但是 $ a^2 + b^2 = c^2 $ 无法被渲染为公式，会保留原字符。但在vscode上用markdown预览器会均显示为公式。看来问题出在空格上，或许是katex要求的latex语法比较严格。但mathjax不会，$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ 和 $ a^2 + b^2 = c^2 $ 都可以渲染为公式 a2+b2=c2a^2 + b^2 = c^2a2+b2=c2。
